frame: local metres about ORIGIN; north -z, east +x

holes.note: Par 4, 386 m, index 10. THE ONLY HOLE THAT CHANGED between the 2020 and 2023 cards — lengthened +31 m from Vit, +14 m from Gul. Bunkering is heavy by this course's standards: five bunkers. A pond sits 14 m right at 84% of the hole — peripheral, not on the line. OSM maps this green fully: 59.56753 N, 16.86843 E, pin node 13012079636. The green is 233 m from the Mälaren shoreline (the second-closest point on the course to water) and 144 m from the clubhouse. A newly built practice area lies immediately BEHIND the first tee, and the club's 18 on-site beds are advertised as 'med första tee och övn
holes.notes: Identified directly from the OSM hole way tagged ref=1 (w1415929746), tee (-62.5,390.7) -> green (-147.2,718.9), par 4, 342 m; corroborated by the banguide, where disc 1 sits NE of the clubhouse and the flag lies SSW of it with hole 2's tee just beyond. Green = OSM green w1415929744 (G0, 568 m2), used verbatim and simplified from 19 to 14 points (area 555 m2). Note the visually pale putting surface in the Esri z18 imagery sits about 5 m WEST of the OSM outline; I kept the surveyed outline rather than the eye-traced one. Fairway traced from a greenness index (G-0.5(R+B)) threshold on z18 tiles: a single continuous mown corridor 24-31 m wide beginning at z~478 (a 75-90 m carry from the back tee, which plays over unmown ground) and running SSW to the green, 5915 m2. The OSM hole way runs along the EAST (player's left) edge of that corridor, not down its middle, so my centreline is the corridor's own middle: it doglegs gently right (west) and measures 336 m. All four bunkers are OSM (fairway bunker (-78,582) on the player's left shoulder; three around the green); a brightness-vs-local-mean sand search over the whole hole found no others. No water anywhere near this hole. Tee pads are the two OSM tee polygons - the back one is a single 26 x 9 m combined teeing ground, angDeg from its own long axis resolved down-line.

holes.note: Par 4, 348 m, index 6. THE CLOSEST HOLE ON THE COURSE TO MÄLAREN — its line of play comes within about 137 m of the shore and the green within 142-144 m. Even so it is not a shoreline hole: a belt of grazed pasture, scrub and a broad reedbed fringe lies between. Water in play is a ditch at the tee and a large 1309 m² pond around the green — corroborated independently by OSM, which maps a golf=lateral_water_hazard (way 1415933872, 1208 m²) just north of this green at 59.56743, 16.87435. OSM green centre 59.56715, 16.87432, pin node 13012115813.
holes.notes: OSM hole way ref=2 (w1415933874): tee (-154.2,786.1) east along the course's south edge to green (190.3,751.3), par 4, 348 m. The banguide agrees exactly - disc 2 is the SW-most marker, the line runs east along the bottom and the flag sits beside disc 3. Green = OSM w1415933870 (G2, 535 m2), simplified 19 -> 14 pts (518 m2). Fairway traced from the greenness mask: one broad corridor 22-27 m of tight fairway (wider mown shoulders) running from x=-33 to the green approach at x=158, with the south edge bulging to z=801 around x=40 where the fairway bunker sits. 4560 m2. Back tee: the OSM polygon w1415933868 straddles a track; the actual mown strip in the imagery is x -166..-129, z 776..785, so I report a 37 x 9 m combined teeing ground centred (-147.5,780.5) - it is one long strip, probably carrying several sets of markers, not several pads. Forward tee is OSM w1415933867 verbatim. Both bunkers are OSM (greenside short-right, fairway bunker right at ~215 m). WATER: an unmapped pond, traced from z18 imagery, lies immediately NORTH/BEYOND the green - smooth uniform surface, bright shoreline on the SW, x 156..206, z 700..731, ~1200 m2. It is only ~4 m past the green's north edge, so it is very much in play on the approach; OSM does not have it, and its colour/texture signature matches the two OSM-mapped ponds near hole 4 in the same imagery. Confidence on the pond outline is medium (the east side merges into dark spruce).

holes.note: Par 3, 179 m, index 8. Longest of the four short holes and one of the straightest on the course (within ~30 m of its tee-green line). The hole-2 tee pond sits behind this tee; a 153 m² pond lies 19 m right at 42%. One bunker. OSM pin node 13012115906 at 59.56837, 16.87134. About 210 m from the shoreline.
holes.notes: OSM hole way ref=3 (w1415933874's neighbour, w1415933877-series): tee (176.1,690.1) -> (19.2,615.8), par 3, 174 m, playing WNW back up the hill from beside the 2nd green. The banguide agrees: disc 3 sits right next to hole 2's red flag and its line runs NW to a flag just south of disc 4 (hole 4's tee at (35.7,533) in OSM), so the routing 2-green -> 3-tee -> 3-green -> 4-tee is confirmed by two independent sources. greenOsmIndex is NULL - this is the one of the four OSM-mapped holes whose GREEN was never drawn (the four OSM green polygons belong to holes 1, 4, 2 and the practice putting green G1 by the clubhouse at (-100,376), area 1017 m2, which is NOT a hole green). Green traced by eye at 9x zoom on z18 imagery: a pale, smooth, slightly yellow-green oval x 1..22, z 599..624, centre (11.4,611.5), 402 m2. I calibrated that signature against the three OSM greens in the same imagery - hole 4's polygon hugs exactly such a pale oval, and hole 1's is a pale oval about 5 m west of its OSM outline. The centre lands 8.8 m NW of the OSM hole way's end point, which is the same order as the way-end/green-centroid offsets on holes 1 (7.4 m) and 4 (3.8 m), so I trust it to about +/-6 m; the green is a bit small (402 vs 490-570 m2 for the mapped ones), so its true edge may run a few metres further out. Fairway: a par 3, but the imagery shows a genuine continuous mown corridor ~28-33 m wide from the green surround out to the forward tee, so I give one ring, x 25..110, 2814 m2, deliberately starting at x=25 to leave the green and its immediate surround out. Single bunker = OSM w1415933878, front-left of the green; the visible sand blob sits about 3 m NW of the OSM polygon but I kept the surveyed ring. Both tees are OSM polygons. WATER: the same unmapped pond as hole 2 (x 156..206, z 700..731) lies immediately south/left of the 3rd tee and is carried on the eye off the tee.

holes.note: Par 4, 337 m, index 2 — the second-hardest hole on the card off a very ordinary length, so the difficulty is entirely in the green complex. TWO PONDS GUARD THE GREEN: 360 m² on the line at 83%, and 410 m² six metres left at 97%. The fairway bends LEFT about 45 m. OSM green 59.57190, 16.87266, pin node 13012116055. The right rough here faces the 5th tee across a mound the club dug out in October 2023.
holes.notes: Fully OSM-mapped (way w1415933888, ref=4, par 4). Banguide disc 4 sits at the south end of the OSM tee strip and the red flag at the OSM green, so the identification is unambiguous. Green ring, greenside bunker (w1415933886) and both tee polygons are the surveyed OSM outlines; the long OSM pad w1415933882 (403 m2, 43 x 9.4 m) is a three-box strip and I split it into white/yellow/blue pads, w1415933881 is the red/orange pad. Distances corroborate the club card (angsogolfklubb.com Scorekort 2020): straight OSM back-tee-to-green = 337.6 m against the card's white 337; near end of the strip = 299 m vs blue 305; forward pad = 228 m vs red 236. My centerline measures 338.5 m. Fairway traced from Esri z18 (0.30 m/px); the corridor is bright mown turf 35-47 m wide climbing NNE from the tee, doglegging right at about (120,330) and turning back left to the green. The two ponds are OSM w1415933883 and w1415933884, hard on the left of the approach and left of the green - very much in play.

holes.note: Par 5, 493 m, index 18 — the easiest hole on the card by index despite being the second-longest, and the ONLY HOLE ON THE COURSE WITH NO BUNKERS AT ALL. Bends LEFT about 80 m. Ponds at 74% and 81% sit on the line. Internal out-of-bounds between 5 and 6 is defined by white/black stakes: 'Dessa pinnar behandlas som föremål för banans gräns under spel av hål 5. Vid spel från hål 6 är de oflyttbara tillverkade föremål' — i.e. the same stakes are a boundary from one hole and an immovable obstruction from the other. An on-course toilet stands here. In Oct 2023 the club dug away the small mound right
holes.notes: Par 5, card white 493 m (yellow 456), index 18. Not in OSM - identified from the banguide: disc 5 sits ENE of the 4th green, its white line runs south down a narrow corridor then swings SE to a flag near disc 6. I registered the banguide raster to the world frame with a least-squares affine on control points that never entered it (the two OSM ponds beside green 4, the S-pond east of hole 6, and the OSM hole-1/2/4 line ends); residuals 1-30 m, and the affine reproduces the OSM hole-4 way to 5-10 m. I then auto-extracted the white hole lines as connected components and traced them, which is the source of the routing. Green: the bright smooth mown blob at (336-364, 611-632) at the end of the corridor, surrounded by trees; the banguide flag-pole base transforms to (349,650), 28 m further south, but for holes 1 and 4 the same pole-base construction lands 7-23 m off the true green centre, so I trust the imagery. A dark tree crown and its shadow sit immediately SE of the green - do not mistake it for part of the putting surface. Tee: the darker irrigated 12 x 34 m strip at x 198-210, z 202-236, about 110 m walk from green 4. My centerline measures 477 m against the card's 493 (3.3% short - the drawn line cuts corners), so the white tee is at or just behind the north end of that strip. The fairway is deliberately asymmetric from z 470 down: a distinct land-cover boundary running (165,443)-(281,569) marks unmown field to the SW, so the corridor is offset NE of the playing line there. One small bunker read just short-right of the green at (350-357, 597-606); no other sand resolved along the corridor, and no water is in play.

holes.note: Par 4, 337 m, index 16. Bends RIGHT about 57 m. A 1003 m² pond crosses the hole at roughly 70% — one of the larger bodies on the course and genuinely on the line. Three bunkers. The right-hand boundary is the electric WILD BOAR FENCE that defines out-of-bounds on holes 6, 7, 16 and 17; beyond it is open arable farmland. About 233 m from the shoreline.
holes.notes: Par 4, card white 337 m, index 16. Not in OSM. Routing from the banguide: disc 6 sits beside the 5th green in the SE corner and its line runs back NNW, bending left round a pond, to a flag that sits immediately beside disc 7 (the 7th tee) - a classic green-to-next-tee pairing, and the strongest confirmation of the identification. The banguide flag-pole base transforms to (327.7,289.1), 12 m from the green centre I traced off the imagery at (319,297), so the green is well constrained. Green complex: the bright smooth mown oval at x 304-334, z 285-310, with the pond and the wooded east flank framing it. Three sand shapes read cleanly on both the z18 and the independent z17 Esri capture: the greenside bunker right-front at (318-331, 313-329), a 28 m crescent fairway bunker at (283-311, 366-377), and a small pot at (276-284, 379-387). The S-shaped pond at (295-341, 363-416) is the hole's defining hazard, on the right of the layup and about 90 m short of the green; I traced its outline from the z18 imagery (it is not in OSM) and it is the same feature I used as an affine control point. Tees: the mown 10 x 50 m strip running NW-SE at (380,551)-(407,591), which lines up along the play direction; back pad placed at its SE end. My centerline measures 346 m against the card's 337 (2.8% long), which brackets the tee position to within about 10 m along the strip. Main residual uncertainty is the exact tee-pad split - individual boxes are not resolvable at 0.30 m/px.

holes.note: Par 5, 545 m, index 4 — the longest hole on the course from every tee, and the BIGGEST DOGLEG: the fairway bends RIGHT by about 103 m at 40% of its length. Essentially dry, with only one small pond 34 m right at 91%. Boar-fence OB down the right. The walk from this green to the 8th tee is about 189 m, the third-longest transfer on the course.
holes.notes: Identified from the banguide: orange disc 7 sits at bg(1290,1482) and its white route line was traced pixel-by-pixel (white connected component) to the flag whose pole base is bg(1231,1042). Registration: a similarity fit banguide-px -> world from five independent OSM anchors (green 1 = OSM w1415929744, green 4 = w1415933887, tee 3, tee 2, tee 4) gives 1.1589 m/px, rotation -0.20 deg, residuals <= 8 m; it predicts green 7 at (256,-230) and tee 7 at (326,280), both of which land on the features traced here. THE HOLE: a long par 5 running north up the eastern corridor against the farm-field edge. Tee complex is tucked in trees at (321-335, 237-265); the drive is played NW over ~120 m of unmown heath before the fairway proper begins near z=165, then the corridor bows west to x~205 around z=40 and swings back NE to the green. Playing length along the centerline 554 m, straight tee-to-green 510 m (bearing 352) - exceptional, but the banguide's own drawn line measures the same, and the transform's scale is corroborated by the OSM anchors. angDeg 315 is the INITIAL line of play off the tee, not the tee-green bearing. Green traced at 621 m2 (OSM greens on this course are 489-1017 m2); its centroid is 16 m north of the banguide pin, within the fit's error. Greenside bunker short-right at (266,-210) is clear sand; the left fairway bunker at (194,86) is a crisp pale oval with a dark lip on the fairway's left edge. Fairway edges are the weakest part: the early-spring imagery makes dormant light rough and fairway hard to separate south of z=100, so widths there are +/-10 m. No water anywhere beside this hole.

holes.note: Par 4, 344 m, index 14. One of the straight holes (within ~30 m of its tee-green line). A pond sits 8 m right at about 53% — close enough to be a visual presence without being a carry.
holes.notes: Identified from the banguide: disc 8 at bg(1113,922), route line traced south (white component 78) to the flag whose pole base is bg(1061,1215). The same similarity fit used for hole 7 predicts tee 8 at (119,-368) and green 8 at (60,-29); the satellite shows the tee strip at (115-127, -383..-329) and the green pad centred (62,-40), so both land within 11 m. A par 4 of 339 m straight, 341 m along the centerline, playing SSW (bearing 190) and bending gently right from x~120 at the tee to x~62 at the green. Three tee pads read as a single 54 m bright strip 11 m wide in a gap between two conifer belts, with the cart path arriving at its south end; the split into three is inferred from the strip's length, not from three separately resolvable pads. Green traced at 630 m2 - the putting surface reads as a rounded, slightly darker and smoother pad just south of the greenside bunker, which is the brightest pale shape on the hole (crisp dark lip on its south edge). The second bunker at (110,-158) is a long left-hand fairway bunker, partly shaded by an overhanging pine; it is definitely pale sand but its south end is guessed under the shadow. The dead-straight thin dark line crossing the fairway near z=-200 is a fence/boundary, not a ditch - no water on this hole.

holes.note: Par 3, 143 m, index 12 — the shortest hole, and from Ora only 55 m, the shortest value on the entire card. A BROOK RUNS RIGHT BY THE GREEN, confirmed twice over: the banguide places a 154 m² water body straddling the line at about 84%, immediately short of the putting surface, and the club's own blog says 'några alar som växer vid bäcken intill green, även detta på hål 9' (Feb 2024, alders by the brook and oaks on the back tee being felled). One bunker. The green is 159 m from the clubhouse and the walk to the 10th tee is only 111 m; the club's kiosk sits at 9/10.
holes.notes: Identified from the banguide: disc 9 at bg(1010,1306) with a short line SSW to the flag whose pole base is bg(971,1423). The similarity fit predicts tee 9 at (1,77) and green 9 at (-44,213); the satellite green pad centroid is (-46,204), 10 m away. A par 3 of 139 m from the back tee (119 m and 98 m from the two forward pads), bearing 196-197, playing SSW down a narrow corridor cut through mature pine, with a cart path running along its west side. Green traced at 562 m2, which matches the OSM-surveyed greens on this course (489-568 m2 for the three single greens); it is the paler, smoother oval clearly separable from its darker collar. Two bunkers: one short-left at (-61,193) and a larger one front-right at (-36,209) with a pronounced shadow lip. IMPORTANT AMBIGUITY RESOLVED: OSM green G1 (index 1, centroid (-100.3,375.9), area 1017 m2) is NOT this hole's green - it lies 180 m SSW, immediately beside OSM's hole-1 tee and just south of the clubhouse, and its size makes it the practice putting green; greenOsmIndex is therefore null. A second decoy is the green-with-large-bunker at about (25,316) near the 1st tee, which no banguide flag reaches and which reads as a practice/chipping complex. The pond at (62-90, 220-256) is ~100 m east of this green, well out of play, so no water is listed. Caution for whoever assembles the 18: the file /root/.claude/uploads/.../72883558-image.webp on disk at one point read back as a DIFFERENT golfisverige.com course than the one the Read tool renders - if PIL-derived banguide pixel coordinates disagree with what you see, re-extract to a uniquely-named file and re-check the disc positions by colour detection.

holes.note: Par 5, 527 m, index 1 — the hardest hole on the card, and remarkably the one hole with NO WATER ANYWHERE IN ITS CORRIDOR. Shaped as a gentle S: left early, then right about 41 m late. One bunker. The 10th tee is 106 m from the clubhouse; in August 2024 the club ran a week-long trial of starting rounds from here (19-25 Aug).
holes.notes: Long straight par 5 (~515 m) running due N-NNE up the western valley from beside the clubhouse/caravan area to a green tucked against the wood at the north end. Identified on the banguide as the long unbroken white line from disc 10 (immediately NE of the clubhouse and its car park / caravan rows) to the red flag ~500 m north; the same line reappears exactly in the satellite as one continuous mown corridor from z~+195 to z~-300 with no break, bounded by forest on the west (the road at x~-215) and a tree belt on the east. Georeferencing came from an affine banguide->world fit on 7 control points (the four OSM hole lines in the south plus two surveyed farm roofs at (-46.5,-685.8) and (37.5,-732.8) in the north); residuals 10-30 m, and the predicted 10th green (-48,-292) landed 17 m from the real bunkered green complex I then traced at 0.30 m/px z18 imagery. Green ~27x32 m (~680 m2), matching the 489-1017 m2 range of the four OSM-surveyed greens. Only one bunker: the large kidney-shaped one hard on the left-front of the green. A soft tan patch at about (-132,-226) mid-fairway is NOT sand - fuzzy edges, dull tone, reads as a worn/dry lie rather than a bunker (the real greenside bunker is bright cream with a crisp rim). Tee complex is a narrow mown tongue running SSW-NNE at x -160..-143, z +160..+205; three pads assumed along it. No water anywhere in the corridor. Fairway width read from the imagery is a generous 45-55 m through the middle, narrowing to the tee.

holes.note: Par 4, 340 m, index 17. SIX BUNKERS — the most on any hole, against a course average of two. Bends RIGHT about 45 m. A 249 m² pond sits at about 21%, squarely in the driving zone. This green to the 12th tee is the LONGEST TRANSFER ON THE COURSE at about 298 m, where the routing crosses between wooded upland blocks.
holes.notes: Par 4 of ~325 m, a gentle dogleg RIGHT: the tee shot plays essentially due north up a corridor at x 5..45, then the hole turns right at about (40,-575) to a green set on a shelf at (92,-653), 75 m east of the club's long white barn at (-46,-686). Identified on the banguide as the line running north out of disc 11 (which sits ~75 m NE of the 10th green) and ending at the red flag just south-east of the two farm roofs; those two roofs were my northern georeferencing control, so this end of the fit is well constrained (predicted green (97,-634) vs traced green centre (92,-653), 21 m). Green ~33x23 m (~590 m2). Six pale, crisp-edged, cream-coloured oval scrapes lie along the corridor and around the green; all read as sand rather than shadow or worn turf, but they are small (5-8 m across) for bunkers, so treat the two furthest from the green (52.5,-598) and (62.7,-572) as the least certain. The tee complex is a narrow mown strip x 14..30 running z -395..-335, partly under tree shadow at its southern (back-tee) end, so the three pads are an interpretation of one continuous mown tongue. No water: the darker patches east of the corridor at x 110..190 are a shaded conifer belt and open farmland, checked at z18, not a pond. Note the routing oddity that the walk from this green to the 12th tee is ~300 m - that is what the banguide itself draws, not an artefact of my fit.

holes.note: Par 3, 169 m, index 9. Water at 25% and again behind the green — a rare back-of-green hazard. One bunker. Sits on the high inland back nine at 12-15 m elevation, 1.4-1.7 km from Mälaren, so no water view at all here.
holes.notes: Par 3 of ~155 m playing NW (bearing ~310 deg) from a tee at about (-85,-905) to a bunkered green at (-199,-1000) in the far north of the course. Identification chain: on the banguide, disc 12 sits at the SE end of a short line running up-left to a red flag; at 7x magnification that flag's pole base is unambiguously where the 12th line terminates, and the SAME point is where the 15th line begins - i.e. this is the northern hub where the 12th green, the 13th tee and the 15th tee all cluster, with the 14th green 55 m further WNW. To confirm it I rendered the satellite into banguide pixel space through the affine and compared: the two bunkered green complexes in the warp fell 20-40 px from the two flags, with the SE one under the 12th flag and the NW one under the 14th flag, and the offsets between the pair matched to ~15 px. Traced green ~30x27 m (~630 m2) with a single crisp cream bunker (~14x7 m) on its SE lip. IMPORTANT: this area is beyond the original z18 tile cache (which stops at z=-474), so I fetched 370 extra Esri tiles (z18 over x -900..400, z -1450..-350 and z17 further north) into angsobuild/cache/sat before tracing; everything here is now read at 0.30 m/px, not from the 1.21 m/px overview. Lowest-confidence element is the tee: the imagery there shows two or three small bright-green pads at x -100..-70, z -935..-885 broken up by a cart path and tree shadow, so the back-tee position (and therefore the hole's length, 130-175 m depending on which pad) is uncertain by ~20 m. The fairway ring is the mown approach corridor SE of the green; it passes south of two tree clumps at (-160,-1008) and (-136,-1022). No water - the nearest pond, at (-395,-920), belongs to the 15th.

holes.note: Par 4, 426 m, index 5 — THE LONGEST PAR 4 on the course by 68 m. Straight (within ~30 m of its line). Ditches lie 30-41 m left at 41% and 58% — well off the corridor. Its green is the HIGH POINT OF THE COURSE at 15.2 m.
holes.notes: Long straight par 5, ~428 m, plays NNW (bearing 325) to the northernmost green on the property. Identification: I registered the club banguide to the world frame with a similarity transform fitted on three OSM green flags in the south (hole 1 green = G0, hole 3 green, hole 4 green = G3); residuals 1-3 m, scale 1.1652 m/banguide-px, rotation -0.36 deg (banguide is north-up). Extrapolated, the banguide's hole-13 flagpole base lands at (-376,-1360) and the satellite shows a distinct smooth rich-green putting surface (auto-detected, 681 m2) centred (-367,-1352) - a 5 m agreement 1500 m from the fit baseline. Same transform confirms neighbours: hole 14 green predicted (-251,-1029) vs detected (-241,-1030); hole 15 green predicted (-381,-903) vs detected (-383,-905); hole 12 green predicted (-206,-999) vs detected (-197,-999). Green is an ellipse fitted to the smooth-turf blob, shrunk to 639 m2 using OSM green G0 as calibration (its visible complex in this Esri imagery is ~2.7x its 568 m2 OSM polygon). Fairway read off a z18 crop (0.30 m/px): a clear 40-46 m wide saturated-green ribbon from z=-1330 to z=-1135; south of that the ground is dormant rough, so there is a ~130 m carry off the tee. Two bunkers: greenside front-left at (-372,-1335) and a small one right of the approach at (-320,-1321), both crisp bright sand. Tees are a 10-15 m mown strip at x -170..-110, z -1090..-975 aligned exactly on the hole axis; back tee at its SE end. Tees are the least certain element (+/- 15 m) since individual pads are not resolvable at 0.3 m/px. No water.

holes.note: Par 4, 350 m, index 11. Bends LEFT about 73 m, the third-strongest turn on the course. A small pond sits 4 m left of the green — very tight to the putting surface. One bunker.
holes.notes: Par 4, ~375 m, a dogleg right: it plays SSE (bearing 167) down the western corridor for ~180 m, then turns hard east along a 20-25 m wide approach to a green that sits about 55 m west of hole 12's green. Identification: the banguide shows hole 14's tee disc immediately west/south of hole 13's green and its line curving south then east; under the transform described for hole 13 the tee disc lands at (-436,-1286), the line start at (-431,-1253) and the flagpole base at (-251,-1029). The satellite shows a smooth rich-green putting surface auto-detected at (-241,-1030) - 10 m from the prediction - with a bright greenside sand bunker at (-263,-1021), and a rounded fairway head at z=-1135 opening into a 35-40 m corridor running due south, exactly matching the drawn route. Chain check: hole 13's green is 120 m from this tee and hole 15's tee is 65 m from this green, so the walking order is coherent. Green (609 m2) is an ellipse fitted to the visible bright surface (x -258..-226, z -1045..-1010) shrunk with the same calibration used on hole 13. The fairway ring is the L: strong saturated green from z=-1135 to z=-1050, then the narrow east approach at z -1052..-1027 out to x=-272. AMBIGUITY: the tee is the weak point. The banguide's disc and its line start differ by 38 m along the axis (unusual - on holes 12, 13 and 15 they coincide), and in the April imagery the tee complex reads only as a 12-14 m wide mown strip at x -428..-416, z -1300..-1225 with no resolvable pads. I placed three pads down that strip with the back tee at (-427,-1282), giving 375 m; if the club's back tee is the strip's south end the hole is nearer 345 m. Everything north of z=-1135 in the corridor is dormant tan rough in this image, so the carry off the tee is long (~150 m); it is possible some of that tan ground is mown fairway that simply had not greened up, in which case the fairway ring should extend further north. No water on this hole.

holes.note: Par 3, 172 m, index 7 — THE WATER HOLE OF THE COURSE AND THE ONLY HOLE WITH A DROP ZONE. The local rules give it its own clause: a YELLOW penalty area, 'Om en boll är i det gula pliktområdet på hål 15 ... droppa den ursprungliga bollen eller en annan boll i droppzonen.' The pond is the LARGEST SINGLE WATER BODY ON THE COURSE at 1828 m², lying directly between tee and green with its near edge on the line of play about 140 m out and the green immediately beyond — verified visually on Esri satellite imagery with the banguide polygons overlaid. From Röd it is 85 m and from Ora 63 m, so the forward
holes.notes: Par 3, ~178 m, plays WSW (bearing 245) across a pond; the tee sits just SW of hole 14's green and hole 16's tee is ~75 m beyond this green, so the chain is coherent. Identification: under the transform described for hole 13, the banguide's hole-15 disc lands at (-228,-974) and its flagpole base at (-381,-903); the satellite has a smooth rich-green putting surface (auto-detected 756 m2) centred (-383,-905), a 2 m agreement. The banguide line at first reads as a sharp dogleg, but a pixel-width measurement settles it: the vertical white segment above the line's western end is 3-4 px wide and 39 px long, matching the flagpole length measured on holes 12 and 14 (40 and 36 px) and half the width of a hole line (7-8 px). So it is the pole, the line is straight, and this is a par 3. WATER: the dark olive blob east of the green is a pond, not turf - RGB (72,85,42) with a local standard deviation of 0.5-1.0 at 0.3 m/px, which no grass surface produces (the adjacent putting green reads 6.6, deep Malaren reads 3.5); 1318 m2, sitting directly on the line of play front/left of the green. The bunker at (-383,-922) is crisp sand with a shadowed south lip on the green's right/back edge. AMBIGUITY: the 'fairway' ring is a genuine mown strip on the north side of the pond (auto-detected as smooth rich turf, 1361 m2) that offers the bail-out left of the carry, but it lies 15-25 m off the straight line, so treat it as an approach/lay-up area rather than a driving fairway - a par 3 here could legitimately be given no fairway at all. Tee positions are the weakest element: mown ground around (-225,-975) is visible but individual pads are not resolvable, so cx/cz are +/- 12 m and the two pads are inferred, not measured. Green shrunk from the detected 756 m2 complex to 588 m2 with the same calibration as holes 13 and 14.

holes.note: Par 4, 338 m, index 13. Bends RIGHT about 71 m. A small 119 m² water body at about 41%. Internal OB in white stakes runs left of both the tee area and the fairway, shared with hole 15 and applying to play on both holes — a sign of how tight these two corridors are. Boar-fence OB down the right against farmland.
holes.notes: Par 4, 338 m from white (club scorecard, index 13). Identified from the club banguide: disc 16 sits at the NW end of a corridor that runs due east then swings hard right (south) to a flag; I registered the banguide to the world frame with a similarity transform fitted on the four OSM-mapped holes (1-4 tee/green pairs, RMS 9.6 m, scale 1.161 m/px, rot +0.3 deg). The transform put green 16 at (-157,-690) and the satellite shows a green complex at (-161,-704) - a 14 m agreement, and my traced centreline measures 338.1 m against the club's printed 338 m, so the identification is solid. Green traced from the smooth bright putting surface (454 m2, in line with the 489-568 m2 OSM greens here); it is the far end of the dogleg, played from the north. Two bunkers: a narrow hooked one hard against the green's N (approach) edge at (-161,-724), and a wedge-shaped one on the green's W side at (-183,-710) - both read as bright smooth low-green patches with the shadowed southern lip that marks a sand hollow in this early-spring imagery. Fairway given as two rings: the main mown corridor from x=-281 east then south to the green (the turf mask picks it out as one 5840 m2 component), plus a thinner, drier mown avenue from the tee east to x=-286 where the turf is broken by shadows and dry patches - the tee shot at 16 carries about 130 m of heath before the fairway proper starts. Tees: only two of the five card tees resolve at 0.30 m/px; the back (white) pad is the 11x7 m patch at (-415,-843). Water: the 1400 m2 pond at (-345,-900) lies 25 m north of the tee-shot line; it primarily guards the 15th green (which sits on its west shore) but is genuinely in play left of 16's tee shot - flagged here so it is not lost, may be duplicated by whoever maps 15.

holes.note: Par 4, 358 m, index 3 — the third-hardest hole and BY FAR THE WETTEST: nine separate water polygons, more than any other hole. A CONTINUOUS RED PENALTY AREA RUNS THE WHOLE LEFT SIDE, and the local rules declare it infinite where it is bounded on one side only: 'Det röda pliktområdet på vänster sida om hål 17 som bara är definierat på en sida är oändligt.' The chain is a meandering ditch plus ponds at roughly 8%, 23%, 51%, 86%, 94% and just past the green, with two ponds left of the green itself. holes.notes: Par 4, 358 m from white (club scorecard, index 3 - the hardest hole on the card). On the banguide disc 17 sits just SW of the 16th green and the line runs straight south down a long narrow tree-walled corridor to a flag in a clearing; the registered banguide put that flag at (-269,-315) and the satellite green complex is at (-269,-322), and my traced centreline measures 359.1 m against the printed 358 m. Green traced at 571 m2 from a distinctly brighter, smoother yellow-green surface ringed by darker fringe - the clearest of my three greens. One bunker: a crisp 58 m2 bright round hollow at (-264,-302), just off the green's S edge, i.e. THROUGH the green for a player coming from the north; it shows the same bright bowl with a shadowed southern lip as the confirmed sand elsewhere, and the club's own summer banguide shows a small pale spot in the same place. Fairway is a single 6900 m2 N-S corridor running z=-576 to z=-340, 20-40 m wide, cut off just north of the green. Water: three features, all with the same signature as ponds I could confirm against the banguide (uniform olive surface, texture sd<1, continuous dark bank) - two small ponds short-right/right of the green at (-253,-343) and (-264,-369) sitting between the corridor and the green, and an elongated 190 m2 pond/wet hollow at (-261,-642) immediately below the tee that the drive must carry or skirt. Medium confidence on the two greenside ponds specifically: they are green rather than blue in the club's summer aerial, so they may be seasonal / weed-covered. Tee complex identified from two mown pads at (-254,-675) and (-243,-656); only 2 of the 5 card tees resolve.

holes.note: Par 5, 497 m, index 15. Bends RIGHT about 55 m off the tee, then straightens for the run home. Water lies just THROUGH the green at 107-111% of the hole length — a hazard that punishes the long third rather than the layup. The green is 126 m from the clubhouse at 5.1 m elevation, closing the descent from the back nine's inland high ground.
holes.notes: Par 5, 497 m from white (club scorecard, index 15) - the closing hole, finishing on the bench just west of the clubhouse and car park. Identified on the banguide as the long line from disc 18 running SSE down the western corridor to a flag beside the clubhouse; the registered flag lands at (-297,348) and the satellite green is at (-294,340), and my traced centreline measures 495.7 m against the printed 497 m, which also pins the back tee: it has to be the mown pad at (-381,-137), not the more obvious one 60 m further down. Green traced at 474 m2 - unusually long and narrow (about 18 x 37 m, N-S) but two independent reads at 0.30 m/px agree, and it sits exactly where the fairway corridor ends. No greenside bunker is visible in either the spring satellite or the club's summer aerial. One fairway bunker, a long narrow 114 m2 sand strip at (-317,163) on the right (west) side at driving-iron range - independently confirmed as white sand in the club's own banguide aerial. Two ponds sitting in the middle of the fairway at (-296,115) and (-284,147): the lower one is unambiguous (it is drawn BLUE in the club's summer aerial), and the upper has an identical dark-water signature in the satellite, so both are water rather than tree clumps. Fairway is one 13700 m2 corridor from z=-55 (the mown ground begins about 90 m off the back tee, after a carry over heath) down to z=315, drifting from x=-355 at the top to x=-305 at the green; it widens east to about x=-256 in the pond belt. Tees: two pads resolve, the white back tee at (-381,-137) and what the card spacing makes the yellow tee at (-358,-84); the blue/red/orange tees are further down the corridor but do not separate from the fairway at this resolution.
